selection.cleanup: Stop starting cases on first unexpected result. Retain first outcome before cleanup. Check exact owned roots and fresh closure; remove only observed matching owned members, bottom-up. Preserve unknown or changed objects and primary errors. Record any descriptor recovery separately. Never retry a case implicitly.
selection.observer_scope: New source-level hooks observe successful descriptor ownership at every compiled sysopen/opendir in the pinned implementation closure, actual closes and explicit observer duplicates. Library-internal native allocations are not attested. Observer recovery remains separate and cannot turn a primary incomplete operation into success.
selection.repeated_observations: Healthy prefix follows the complete-file policy; the selected negative operation and explicit maintenance follow-up do not add implicit reuse calls.
selection.scope: Prospective source-bound selection only. Harness, independent journal reader and final execution admission are still unqualified.
selection.shared_base_policy: Execution establishes these common project artifact bases through the existing locality helper. They are shared infrastructure and are excluded from exclusive case-root cleanup; no existing shared contents are deleted.
selection.wall_scope: Perl case and cleanup alarms plus an overall monotonic budget check bound ordinary execution. Journal failure preserves fixture roots. This does not certify cleanup after interpreter loss or a kernel-uninterruptible call; such incomplete outcomes remain failures.
